gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much weight an extender puts on the laptop lid compared with the screen area it adds: the Mobile Pixels Duex Max DS hangs 1.8 lb on the back of the lid for 84.9 sq in of screen (47.2 sq in per lb), while ASUS's 15.6-inch ZenScreen MB169CK portable monitor gives 104.0 sq in for 1.72 lb that sits on the table (60.5 sq in per lb), with 0 lb on the hinge.
standout_why: I compared against Best Buy Canada (cited; its readable part is a product grid with CAD prices and no weights or ratios), ViewSonic's dual-screen guide (cited; it gives only its own VG1457 weight of 2.6 lb and says in words that extenders 'add weight directly onto the laptop', with no number for the load on the lid), and bestusefultips (cited; it has no weights, prices or ratios and only says to check hinge strength). None of them puts a weight on the load an extender puts on the lid, and none gives screen area per pound or compares the two types. I could not open WorkChoose (TLS certificate error).
decides: This backs ChatGPT's default pick of a portable monitor for one added screen. A single 15.6-inch portable monitor weighs less than the 14.1-inch attachable screen and has 22% more area, and none of its weight is on the hinge. Extenders win only on fewer pieces to set up and a smaller footprint in tight spaces, not on screen per pound. Clamped dual extenders are the worst case: The Gadgeteer put a FOPO 15-inch triple at 7+ lb on the lid, which works out to at most 27.5 sq in per lb. Whether a screen works with the laptop's video ports still decides fit first. This finding only ranks the screens that fit.

findings.label: Weight carried on the laptop lid
findings.value: 1.8 lb (0.8 kg), all of it on the lid
findings.source_title: Hands-on review: Mobile Pixels Duex Max DS – time to double up (FutureFive, Owen McCarthy, 2024-02-19)
findings.note: Owen McCarthy quotes '1.8 lbs (0.8kg)' from the technical specifications. He writes that it 'clips to your laptop magnetically', with magnets stuck to the rear of the lid, so the lid and hinge carry the full weight. The maker's page returned HTTP 429 on every try.

findings.label: Added screen area per lb carried
findings.source_title: Hands-on review: Mobile Pixels Duex Max DS – time to double up (FutureFive)
findings.note: Area at 14.1 in, 16:9 = 14.1² × 144/337 = 84.9 sq in; 84.9 ÷ 1.8 lb = 47.2 sq in/lb. The 14.1-inch 1920×1080 16:9 spec is from our product record.

findings.label: Net weight without stand
findings.value: 0.78 kg (1.72 lb), 0 lb on the laptop lid
findings.note: ASUS: 'Net Weight without Stand : 0.78 kg (1.72 lbs)'; panel 15.6 in 1920×1080, 250 cd/m², power consumption 7.64 W. Video path: 'USB-C x 2 (DP Alt Mode)' plus 'Mini HDMI x 1', so it needs no driver on a laptop with a video-capable USB-C port. It stands on its own, so none of its weight is on the hinge.

findings.label: Added screen area per lb carried
findings.note: 15.6² × 144/337 = 104.0 sq in; 104.0 ÷ 1.72 lb = 60.5 sq in/lb. Compared with the Duex Max DS: 104.0 ÷ 84.9 = 1.22, so 22% more screen, while weighing 0.08 lb less in total and putting 0 lb on the lid.

findings.label: Added screen area per lb carried (dual 14-inch, folding, freestanding)
findings.value: 67.8 sq in/lb (176.2 sq in for 2.6 lb)
findings.source_title: Complete Guide to Dual-Screen Portable Monitors | ViewSonic
findings.note: ViewSonic: two 14-inch WUXGA (1920×1200, 16:10) panels, 2.6 lb for the whole setup, 65 W USB-C PD. Per panel 14² × 160/356 = 88.1 sq in; × 2 = 176.2 sq in; ÷ 2.6 lb = 67.8 sq in/lb. It folds flat and stands apart from the laptop, so it puts 0 lb on the lid.

findings.product: FOPO 15-inch Triple Portable Monitor (2 × 15-inch, older model)
findings.label: Lid-clamped dual extender: screen area per lb
findings.value: at most 27.5 sq in/lb (192.3 sq in for 7+ lb)
findings.source_title: FOPO 15 Inch Triple Portable Monitor review – with many monitors comes many cables (The Gadgeteer, Matt Gregersen, 2023-06-18)
findings.note: Matt Gregersen gives the weight as '7+ pounds' for two added 15-inch 1920×1080 panels clamped to the lid with spring brackets. He says the kickstand helps 'if your hinge can't take the extra weight'. It needs one video-capable USB-C port per screen; his Asus G18 had only one, so one side needed HDMI plus a USB-C power cable. Per panel 15² × 144/337 = 96.1 sq in; × 2 = 192.3 sq in; ÷ 7 lb = 27.5 sq in/lb (an upper bound, because the weight is '7+').
